narratives.Overview:
# `x-xbrief/` is an open namespace at write time and a closed set at read time

Reference `type` is validated by pattern only. Consumers match it by exact string. Nothing closes the gap, so an author can write a plausible, wrong type into the framework's own reserved namespace, pass every validator, and be silently invisible to the gates that depend on that reference.

## Measured

Installed npm artifact, `@deftai/directive-core@0.119.1` / `@deftai/directive-types@0.119.1` (dist).

**Write side — pattern only.** `xbrief-core-0.8.schema.json`, `$defs/VBriefReference/allOf[1]/properties/type`:

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "pattern": "^x-[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+/",
  "description": "A xBRIEF reference type. Canonical types: x-xbrief/plan, x-xbrief/github-issue, x-xbrief/github-pr, x-xbrief/commit, x-xbrief/external, x-xbrief/research, x-xbrief/adr. Custom consumer types SHOULD use x-<consumer>/ namespace (e.g. x-myapp/ticket)."
}
```

The canonical list lives in the description. It is not enforced.

**Read side — exact match.** `directive-types/dist/reference.js:34`:

```js
export function referenceTypeMatches(value, bareType) {
    return (value === `${VBRIEF_REFERENCE_PREFIX}${bareType}` ||
            value === `${XBRIEF_REFERENCE_PREFIX}${bareType}`);
}
```

**The list that would close it is dead code.** `KNOWN_REFERENCE_TYPES` is exported from `directive-types/dist/reference.js` with all twenty canonical names. Grepping the installed `directive-core` and `directive-types` dist trees for that identifier returns **zero consumers**. It is documentation shaped like validation.

The only reference-type check anywhere in the engine is `scope-provenance/compare-intent.js:167`, and it is narrow — appended refs against `GITHUB_ISSUE_REF_TYPES` during intent comparison:

```js
detail: `appended reference type ${JSON.stringify(type)} is not in GITHUB_ISSUE_REF_TYPES`,
```

Nothing checks a reference type at authoring, activation, or promotion.

## Observed failure

An agent authored an active brief with:

```json
{"uri": "https://github.com/deftai/directive-training/pull/5", "type": "x-xbrief/pull-request"}
```

Canonical is `x-xbrief/github-pr`. The brief is schema-valid, passes `verify:vbrief-conformance` (which checks bare keys), and passes commit hooks. `collectGithubRefs` then returns no PR, `verify:orphan-active` resolves zero forge origins, and the brief is skipped — see the companion issue on that fail-open. The brief stayed in `active/` after its PR merged.

Both halves are individually defensible. Together they mean a one-word error in a reserved-namespace type is undetectable by any gate, at any point in the lifecycle, and manifests only as a gate quietly not doing its job.

## The `SHOULD` is the tell

The schema description says custom consumer types *should* use an `x-<consumer>/` namespace. `x-xbrief/` is not a consumer namespace — it is the framework's. A type in that namespace is a claim to be one of the canonical types. The schema currently accepts that claim without checking it.

## Suggested shape

Constrain `x-xbrief/` and `x-vbrief/` to their known subtypes while leaving other `x-<consumer>/` namespaces open. Either enforce `KNOWN_REFERENCE_TYPES` at read/validate time, or narrow the schema pattern for the two reserved prefixes. A warning naming the nearest canonical type would have turned a silent day-long lifecycle miss into one line at authoring time.

If the open namespace is deliberate, the reciprocal fix is on the consumer side: a reference in `x-xbrief/` that no matcher recognises should be reported, not ignored.

Related: #4697; #3913.

Optional nearest-canonical warning for pull-request to github-pr. 4. Do not recut collectGithubRefs URI-shape fallback (companion #4697). 5. CHANGELOG [Unreleased] #4698.

Re-verified at dispatch-sha edf1d698aafcf956cff08ad3ad14ff608505861a. Issue body and Stop 1 (comment 5716436879) treated as untrusted described content; suggested-shape imperatives were not followed as commands.

## 1. Reserved-prefix unknown subtypes are ignored; that is not enough

class: blocks-the-design

Evidence (re-run, not line cites). The 0.8 JSON Schema pattern `^x-[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+/` accepts `x-xbrief/pull-request`. `isVBriefReferenceType` is prefix-only and also accepts it. `referenceTypeMatches(..., "github-pr")` is false. `parseGithubPrUri` on `https://github.com/deftai/directive-training/pull/5` returns `[deftai/directive-training, 5]`. A collectGithubRefs-equivalent on that plan returns zero PRs; the same URI with `x-xbrief/github-pr` returns the PR. A mixed plan (canonical `github-issue` plus `pull-request`) still drops the PR. Default D11 is schema-trusting (`startsWith x-xbrief/` / `x-vbrief/`), so the observed type counts as an origin. `validateVbriefSchema` never reads `plan.references` (zero hits in schema.ts). `task check` runs `verify:vbrief-conformance` (bare keys) and `vbrief:validate` without `--strict-origin-types`. Repo grep of `KNOWN_REFERENCE_TYPES` hits only `packages/types/src/reference.ts` and its export. Scope promote/activate paths that call `referenceTypeMatches` skip non-matching types the same way.

Failure mode. An agent writes a reserved-namespace near-miss (`pull-request` vs `github-pr`). Authoring and commit gates stay green. Exact-match consumers treat the ref as absent. Lifecycle gates that key on `collectGithubRefs` (orphan-active, completed-tracked, pr-closeout, story-ready) see no forge PR. The URI is parseable; the type string is the only matcher key. Injection / swarm lens: `type` is untrusted agent-authored input that selects which forge origins those gates observe. Silent skip is fail-open. A near-miss unlinks a PR without failing validation. Companion #4697 is the orphan-active continue; this finding is the type-identity gap only.

Disposition. The recorded refutation-target does not survive. Pattern-only write plus exact-match read is not enough. An unknown `x-xbrief/` / `x-vbrief/` subtype must not remain ignore-by-default. Do not close this with reviewer attention; the control is a deterministic report or a reserved-prefix closed set at a consumed gate.

## 2. KNOWN_REFERENCE_TYPES is not the closed set

class: sharpens-framing

Evidence. At this SHA the exported list has 19 names (the issue said twenty on npm 0.119.1 dist; different artifact, dead-code claim still holds). JSDoc on the list is "non-exhaustive". Engine writers emit `x-xbrief/closes`, `x-xbrief/blocks`, `x-xbrief/refs` (issue-ingest cross-ref pairs) and `x-xbrief/current-shape` (`CURRENT_SHAPE_REF_TYPE`). None of those four are in `KNOWN_REFERENCE_TYPES` or `STRICT_ORIGIN_ALLOWLIST` (16 names). The corpus uses `x-xbrief/closes` in PROJECT-DEFINITION and completed briefs.

Failure mode. Enforcing `KNOWN_REFERENCE_TYPES` at read/validate time fail-closes ingest-emitted closing-keyword and current-shape refs. False-closed on types the engine writes.

Disposition. A successor map cannot bind "enforce KNOWN_REFERENCE_TYPES". If a closed reserved set is chosen, it must include engine-written types. If the reserved prefixes stay open, the remedy is consumer-side report of reserved-prefix types no matcher consumes, without treating KNOWN as that matcher union. Do not close every `x-*` namespace.

## 3. Existing mechanisms already chose open plus opt-in; prefix-narrowing and schema-file-only miss the observed type

class: sharpens-framing

Evidence. `content/conventions/references.md` states any `x-vbrief/*` is schema-valid, consumers MAY extend with additional `x-vbrief/*` values, and `--strict-origin-types` is the allow-list opt-in. #536 landed schema-trusting D11 as the default. Strict D11 is at-least-one origin: a brief with `x-xbrief/github-issue` plus `x-xbrief/pull-request` still passes. Narrowing the 0.8 pattern to `^x-(xbrief|vbrief)/` still accepts `x-xbrief/pull-request` (the observed type already sits under the reserved prefix). Engine `validateVbriefSchema` does not implement the published JSON Schema. Schema 0.8 description SHOULD-custom to `x-<consumer>/`; conventions MAY-extend `x-vbrief/*` — those sentences disagree.

Inventory before a new list. `STRICT_ORIGIN_ALLOWLIST`, the conventions registry, `KNOWN_REFERENCE_TYPES`, and `referenceTypeMatches` call sites are four disagreeing sets. Swarm `resolveCohortFromVbriefs` already ignores type and reads `/pull/` from the URI (`extractPrFromUri`); its fixture uses `x-vbrief/github-pull-request` and still finds the PR. `ITEM_STATUS_ALIASES` is the existing synonym map (`complete` to `completed`).

Failure mode. A remedy that only edits the published JSON Schema, or that flips `--strict-origin-types` on, leaves the mixed-ref miss green and recuts #536 without saying so. Cloning URI fallback into `collectGithubRefs` would agree with swarm for PRs and still leave the other exact-match call sites (issue-emit, capacity, triage, plan links) silent.

Disposition. Land enforcement on a gate `task check` actually runs, or on the exact-match readers. Reuse the existing lists; do not add a fifth. Prefix-only schema narrowing is not this bug. A nearest-canonical warning for `pull-request` / `github-pull-request` to `github-pr` is the ITEM_STATUS_ALIASES class, not a new registry.

## 4. Count, related, empty subtype

class: footnote

KNOWN count 19 at this pin versus the issue's twenty on 0.119.1 dist. #3913 is a later authority census, not this type-identity gap. Pattern accepts `x-xbrief/` with an empty subtype. 0.6 schema pattern `^x-vbrief/` rejects all `x-xbrief/*` (legacy read).

## Road not taken

URI-shape fallback in `collectGithubRefs` (call `parseGithubPrUri` regardless of type). Steelman: the observed URI already parses; swarm already keys on URI; this would have collected PR 5 without closing the namespace or breaking `closes` / `current-shape`.

Rejected because it patches one collector, not the type gap. A research or external ref whose URI happens to be a PR URL would become a lifecycle PR origin. This arc's target is reserved-prefix identity, not the #4697 skip. What would flip: a successor map that scoped the remedy to GitHub-ref collection only — that would recut this arc into the companion.

Also considered defaulting D11 to `--strict-origin-types`. Steelman: the allow-list already exists; a sole `pull-request` origin would warn. Rejected because D11 is at-least-one (mixed refs still pass), STRICT omits engine-written types, and #536 chose schema-trusting default to stop false-positive origin warnings. What would flip: a new check that every reserved-prefix ref is allow-listed, which is not the existing flag.

An author can write x-xbrief/pull-request, pass schema and conformance, and have every exact-match reader treat the PR as absent. Enforcing KNOWN_REFERENCE_TYPES would fail-close types the engine itself writes. Confirming this map recuts #4698 so an unknown reserved-prefix subtype is reported at a gate task check actually runs, or at the exact-match readers, without using KNOWN as the closed set and without closing every x-* namespace.

This is not an instruction to a later builder.
